title: Siit Review 2026: Honest Pros and Cons for Internal Support Teams
summary: Explore Siit’s features, pricing, AI, workflows, and integrations, and compare Siit vs. Unthread for scalable internal employee support.
body_text: Siit is an employee service management platform for organizations that want to centralize employee requests, automate internal workflows, and coordinate service delivery across IT, HR, finance, legal, facilities, and operations. Its product combines conversational intake, service catalogs, approvals, knowledge management, integrations, reporting, asset and SaaS visibility, and AI capabilities for employee support. For internal support teams, the decision is not only whether Siit can turn employee questions into tickets. Buyers also need to understand how requests move through Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and the portal; how private and cross-department work is handled; which AI and workflow features are included by plan; and how much administration is required after launch. This review examines Siit’s capabilities, pricing, strengths, and key evaluation considerations, then compares its approach with Unthread for internal support teams. Key Takeaways Siit supports employee service delivery across IT, HR, finance, legal, facilities, and operations through Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and self-service workflows. Its main strengths include structured service catalogs, request forms, approvals, cross-department routing, native collaboration-tool intake, and admin-based pricing with unlimited employee requesters. Teams should test public and private request handling, workflow depth, AI controls, integrations, reporting, and ongoing administration with representative internal workflows. Siit and Unthread both support conversational internal help desks, but they differ in pricing model, channel emphasis, AI approach, workflow administration, and broader ITSM capabilities. The right choice depends on where employees ask for help, how many departments share the platform, and how much configuration the internal team can maintain over time. What Is Siit? Siit positions itself as an employee service management platform rather than a tool limited to IT ticketing. Organizations can use it to receive, route, approve, track, and report on requests across several internal departments. Typical examples include software access, equipment requests, onboarding tasks, benefits questions, expense issues, legal reviews, facilities work, and workplace operations. Employees can submit requests through Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, or a self-service portal. Administrators can manage requests through connected collaboration threads and Siit’s centralized service workspace. The request conversation keeps replies, internal notes, approvals, SLA updates, assignments, and workflow events in one timeline while synchronizing updates back to the employee’s original channel. Core Siit capabilities include: Request management for internal employee support Native Slack and Microsoft Teams intake, plus email and portal options Service catalogs, service forms, approvals, routing, and SLAs Public and private request handling with department-specific access Knowledge integrations and article suggestions Reporting, analytics, asset management, and SaaS management Integrations with HR, identity, device-management, ticketing, and workplace systems AI Assist, AI Triage, and plan-dependent AI agents for answers, routing, and workflow execution Siit Pricing and Total Cost Siit publishes admin-based pricing starting at $23 per admin per month for Essentials, $45 for Standard, and $89 for Pro when billed annually. Employee requesters are unlimited, a custom enterprise plan is available, and Siit offers a 14-day free trial. Teams should confirm current feature availability, implementation support, integrations, usage limits, and security requirements before calculating total cost. The pricing model can be attractive when many employees submit requests but only a smaller group administers the platform. Total cost still depends on the number of admins, the plan required for AI agents and advanced workflows, implementation effort, integration work, documentation cleanup, and ongoing workflow maintenance. Siit Review: Pros and Considerations What Siit Does Well Siit provides a broad employee-service model across multiple departments. Service catalogs and forms can standardize repeatable requests, while routing, approvals, SLAs, and team inboxes help make ownership visible. This is useful for organizations moving away from scattered chat messages, shared inboxes, and informal handoffs. Its native collaboration integrations are another strength. In Slack, employees can mention Siit in public channels, message the app privately, or turn an existing message into a request. Status changes, assignments, and resolutions can appear in the same thread. Microsoft Teams users can create private requests, convert messages into tickets, complete adaptive forms, and receive status updates without leaving Teams. Siit also supports public and private service flows. Public requests can remain discoverable in a shared channel, while sensitive HR, security, or employee-relations matters can move to a private conversation with restricted visibility. This helps teams use conversational intake without treating every request as public. What Teams Should Evaluate Teams evaluating Siit should test: Public and private request handling in Slack and Microsoft Teams Department-specific roles, permissions, service ownership, and reporting Workflow configuration, approval depth, dependencies, and escalation behavior AI availability, knowledge grounding, confidence controls, and human handoff by plan Integration behavior with existing HRIS, MDM, identity, asset, and ticketing systems The effort required to maintain workflows, knowledge, routing, forms, and service catalogs after launch The full annual cost based on admin count, plan selection, implementation, and support needs Testing should include real examples from IT, HR, finance, legal, procurement, facilities, and workplace operations. A short demo may show ticket creation, but it may not reveal how the system handles confidential requests, multi-step approvals, cross-team dependencies, or changes to workflows after implementation. AI, Knowledge, and Workflow Automation Siit’s AI capabilities include knowledge-based answers, triage, routing, and plan-dependent AI agents that can execute supported actions. For IT workflows, its documentation describes agent actions for systems such as Okta, JumpCloud, Slack, Jira, Zendesk, and webhooks, with approval gates available for sensitive steps. Teams should distinguish between answer generation, ticket deflection, and completed resolution. Showing an employee a policy article is different from collecting missing details, obtaining approval, updating a connected system, confirming completion, and closing the request. Buyers should measure these outcomes separately during a pilot. Knowledge quality remains important because inaccurate or outdated documentation can weaken AI performance. Teams should review how Siit connects to sources such as Notion, Confluence, SharePoint, or Microsoft 365, how citations are shown, and how proposed updates are reviewed before they become trusted guidance. Channels, Workflows, and Administration Siit supports creating and managing service requests directly in Slack, including: Public-channel mentions Private messages Message actions Threaded updates Assignments Status notifications Slack-first teams should test the complete experience for intake, triage, workflow execution, private requests, escalation, and human handoff. The same evaluation should be repeated in Microsoft Teams and email. Teams should verify: How forms, attachments, replies, approvals, and status updates synchronize across channels Whether the original context remains visible when a request moves between departments Administration is another major consideration. Internal processes change as teams add locations, systems, approvers, policies, and service targets. Buyers should test whether non-technical administrators can update: Services Forms Routing Permissions SLAs Workflows Knowledge They should be able to make these updates without creating a long engineering queue or relying on repeated professional-services work. How Conversational Internal Help Desks Differ Conversational internal help desks allow employees to submit and follow requests through familiar collaboration tools. The important differences are: How deeply ticket management remains in chat Which channels are supported How AI executes workflows How private requests are protected How easily administrators can maintain routing, approvals, and integrations Siit emphasizes native support across Slack and Microsoft Teams, structured service catalogs, admin-based pricing, and a centralized employee-service workspace. Unthread emphasizes a Slack-centered internal help desk, purpose-built AI agents, lower ongoing configuration overhead, and a broader combination of: Knowledge Workflow automation SLA and SLO tracking Incident and change management On-call rotations Analytics API access Webhooks Unthread as a Siit Alternative Unthread turns collaboration-channel requests into one Slack-based internal help desk for: IT HR Finance Procurement Legal Workplace operations Other internal teams Employee messages become structured tickets with ownership, routing, service targets, approvals, privacy controls, and complete conversation context. Its purpose-built AI agents can: Answer from approved documentation Collect missing information Classify and route requests Trigger supported actions Escalate work with the original conversation attached Unthread customer examples report 40% automatic resolution across internal teams when knowledge and workflows are in place. Unthread also includes an automation builder for: Approvals Provisioning Escalations Notifications Connected-system actions Its knowledge management capabilities identify documentation gaps and help teams keep internal guidance current as requests are resolved. This model may fit organizations that want employees to stay in familiar collaboration tools while giving internal teams one operating model for: Ticketing AI Knowledge SLAs Analytics Incidents Changes On-call work Integrations Custom agentic prompts Why Unthread Is the Stronger Choice for Internal Support For organizations modernizing internal support, the most important question is not simply whether a platform can create tickets. Teams need a system that can manage employee requests from intake through resolution while keeping workflows easy to maintain as departments, policies, approvers, and service targets change. Unthread provides a unified internal help desk for IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, workplace operations, and other internal teams. Its Slack-based help desk turns employee messages, private requests, emails, and other intake sources into structured tickets with ownership, routing, approvals, privacy controls, and complete conversation context. Unthread’s purpose-built AI agents support more than basic question answering. They can use approved documentation, collect missing information, classify and route requests, trigger supported workflows, and escalate tickets with the original conversation attached. This allows internal teams to automate repeatable Tier 1 workflows while maintaining human oversight for sensitive or complex requests. The platform also brings essential internal service management capabilities into one operating model, including: Ticketing and request routing Workflow automation Approvals and connected-system actions Knowledge management SLA and SLO tracking Analytics and reporting Incident and change management On-call rotations API access and webhooks Custom agentic prompts This connected approach helps teams avoid managing separate systems for conversational intake, ticketing, knowledge, automation, and ITSM operations. It also gives non-technical administrators more control over routing rules, forms, workflows, and service processes without creating a growing engineering backlog. For Slack-first organizations that want employees to request help without leaving their existing workspace, Unthread provides a stronger long-term foundation. Its combination of structured ticketing, AI-driven automation, internal knowledge, workflow management, and broader ITSM capabilities makes it well suited for teams that want to improve resolution speed, reduce manual triage, and scale internal service delivery across departments. Frequently Asked Questions Is Siit a good fit for internal support teams? Siit may fit organizations that want employee service management across several departments, native Slack and Microsoft Teams intake, service catalogs, approvals, AI agents, and admin-based pricing. Teams should validate the plan required for their workflows, integrations, reporting, permissions, and support expectations. Can Siit manage private HR or security requests? Yes. Siit supports public and private requests. Sensitive requests can move to a direct conversation with restricted visibility, while authorized agents continue managing the work through the service workspace. Teams should test permission changes, approvals, audit history, and retention requirements for confidential workflows. How is Siit different from Unthread? Both platforms support conversational internal service delivery. Siit emphasizes native Slack and Microsoft Teams experiences, service catalogs, admin-based pricing, and asset or SaaS management. Unthread emphasizes its Slack-centered internal help desk, purpose-built AI agents, knowledge management, lower configuration overhead, and broader internal ITSM functions such as incidents, changes, and on-call rotations. What should teams test during a Siit pilot? Use representative requests from IT, HR, finance, legal, facilities, and operations. Measure ticket creation, privacy, routing, approvals, AI accuracy, automated actions, human handoff, SLA tracking, reporting, and the time required to update workflows or knowledge after the pilot begins. When should teams compare Unthread? Teams may compare Unthread when they want one internal-support model across departments, purpose-built AI agents for repeatable Tier 1 workflows, easier ongoing configuration, and connected ticketing, knowledge, automation, analytics, incidents, changes, on-call operations, APIs, and webhooks.

title: Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports Microsoft SQL Server 2025
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports Microsoft SQL Server 2025
body_text: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports Microsoft SQL Server 2025 for Enterprise, Standard, and Developer editions. SQL Server 2025 brings AI integration directly into the database engine, enabling customers to invoke external REST endpoints from T-SQL without additional middleware. Customers running RDS for SQL Server can use this capability to integrate existing database workloads securely with AWS services such as Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, Amazon S3, and AWS Lambda, without re-architecting applications. This enables scenarios such as AI-powered query advisor, automated performance analysis, event-driven workflows, and calling custom web services on Amazon EC2. SQL Server 2025 introduces a new free edition for development and testing without licensing costs (Standard Developer Edition, or Dev-SE), and significant Standard Edition capacity increases up to 32 cores and 256 GB buffer pool memory. Standard Edition also gains Resource Governor, previously exclusive to Enterprise Edition. SQL Server 2025 also introduces a native vector data type for storing and querying vector embeddings directly within the database. Customers running earlier SQL Server versions on RDS can upgrade to SQL Server 2025 by modifying the DB engine version, and customers running SQL Server on premises can migrate to take advantage of these capabilities with fully managed infrastructure. For more information, see the Amazon RDS for SQL Server User Guide . See Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing for up-to-date pricing and regional availability.

title: Introducing: SunSmart Stabilizer
summary: Introducing SunSmart Stabilizer! This pool stabilizer offers a new way to protect your chlorine without contributing to CYA buildup.
body_text: Chlorine works hard to keep your pool clean and safe. But on sunny days, ultraviolet rays can break down unprotected chlorine quickly. Traditional pool stabilizers help prevent this chlorine loss, but they also add cyanuric acid, or CYA, to the water. If CYA levels climb too high, chlorine becomes less effective and restoring balance may require partially draining and refilling the pool. SunSmart Stabilizer offers another way to protect your chlorine. Its proprietary, CYA-free formula helps chlorine last longer in sunlight without contributing to CYA buildup. Table of Contents What Is SunSmart Stabilizer? Why Is CYA Buildup a Problem? How Does SunSmart Stabilizer Work? How to Use SunSmart Stabilizer Using SunSmart Stabilizer in Saltwater Pools Benefits of SunSmart Stabilizer Helps Chlorine Last Longer Avoids Additional CYA Buildup Helps Prevent Algae Supports Clearer Water May Reduce Chemical Use Great for Saltwater Pools A Smarter Approach to Chlorine Care What Is SunSmart Stabilizer? SunSmart Stabilizer is a liquid pool water stabilizer designed to shield chlorine from the effects of UV rays. Think of it like sunscreen for your sanitizer. By slowing chlorine loss caused by sunlight, SunSmart helps chlorine stay in the water longer and work more efficiently. Unlike traditional stabilizers, SunSmart provides UV protection without raising the pool’s CYA level. This makes it especially useful for saltwater pools and pools that regularly use stabilized chlorine products. Why Is CYA Buildup a Problem? CYA is not always bad. At the proper level, between 30-100 ppm, it protects chlorine from sunlight and helps maintain a consistent sanitizer residual. The problem occurs when too much CYA accumulates. Stabilized chlorine products, including trichlor tabs and dichlor shock, add a small amount of CYA each time they are used. Because CYA does not evaporate or break down quickly, it gradually builds up in the water. When CYA levels get too high, chlorine becomes less effective. This can lead to: Increased chlorine demand Cloudy or dull water Greater risk of algae growth More complicated water care The need to partially or fully drain and refill the pool SunSmart Stabilizer helps reduce reliance on traditional CYA-based stabilizers, making it easier to manage CYA levels over time. How Does SunSmart Stabilizer Work? SunSmart works the same way a traditional stabilizer does, by forming a protective barrier around the chlorine molecules and shielding them from the sun. With less chlorine being broken down by UV rays, more sanitizer remains available to fight bacteria, algae, and other contaminants. This can help maintain a steadier chlorine level, especially during hot, sunny weather or periods of heavy pool use. SunSmart Stabilizer differs from traditional stabilizers by using 0.25% titanium dioxide instead of CYA. Titanium dioxide provides dual benefits to your pool water. In addition to protecting chlorine molecules from UV damage, it's also a catalytic oxidizer. Which, in simple terms, means when UV light hits the titanium dioxide particle, it creates short-lived oxidizers that quickly kill organic contaminants in the water. This combo means your chlorine stays protected from the sun and lasts longer thanks to fewer contaminants in the water. However, even with all these great benefits, remember that SunSmart does not replace chlorine, shock, or routine water balancing. Instead, it supports your sanitizer and helps it work more efficiently. How to Use SunSmart Stabilizer The initial dose is 1 gallon of SunSmart Stabilizer per 10,000 gallons of pool water. For continued protection, add 1/2 gallon per 10,000 gallons each month. Always follow the product label and confirm your pool’s volume before dosing. Keep the circulation system running as directed to help distribute the product throughout the water. Using SunSmart Stabilizer in Saltwater Pools Saltwater pools generate chlorine instead of relying on chlorine tabs for everyday sanitizing, but that chlorine is still vulnerable to sunlight. Traditionally, saltwater pool owners add a CYA-based stabilizer to protect the chlorine from UV rays. SunSmart provides that UV protection without adding CYA. This removes the need to regularly add traditional CYA-based stabilizers, drastically reducing the risk of CYA buildup over time. Using SunSmart may also help the salt chlorine generator operate more efficiently. When chlorine lasts longer in the water, the system does not have to work as hard to maintain the proper sanitizer level. This can simplify water care while helping protect the life of the salt cell. Keep in mind that SunSmart will not remove CYA already in the pool. Pool owners should continue testing their CYA and chlorine levels regularly. Benefits of SunSmart Stabilizer If you're looking for a different way to protect your chlorine and pool, SunSmart Stabilizer deserves a spot at the top of your list. Just take a look at all the ways it benefits your pool: Helps Chlorine Last Longer Direct sunlight can quickly reduce the amount of available chlorine in an outdoor pool. SunSmart protects against UV loss so your chlorine stays active longer. Avoids Additional CYA Buildup SunSmart provides chlorine protection without adding more CYA to the water. This gives pool owners greater control over their stabilizer level and helps prevent problems associated with excessive CYA. Helps Prevent Algae When chlorine levels fall too low, algae can gain a foothold. By helping maintain a more consistent sanitizer level, SunSmart supports proactive algae prevention. Supports Clearer Water Efficient chlorine performance helps control the contaminants that can make pool water look cloudy or dull. SunSmart helps your sanitizer keep up during hot weather and heavy swimming periods. May Reduce Chemical Use Because less chlorine is lost to sunlight, you may not need to replenish it as frequently. More efficient sanitizer use can make routine pool care simpler and may help lower chemical costs over time. Great for Saltwater Pools Saltwater pools generate their own chlorine, but that chlorine is still vulnerable to UV rays. SunSmart helps protect it without increasing CYA, allowing the salt system to operate more efficiently. A Smarter Approach to Chlorine Care SunSmart Stabilizer helps solve a common pool care challenge: protecting chlorine from sunlight without allowing CYA to build up over time. By helping chlorine last longer and work more effectively, it can support clearer water, simpler maintenance, and more reliable algae prevention. Whether you have a traditional chlorine pool or a saltwater system, SunSmart Stabilizer can help you spend less time managing your sanitizer and more time enjoying the water. title: PPHC Strengthens Public Affairs Offering with Hire of Managing Director and Content Specialist
summary: WASHINGTON, July 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — PPHC (“the Company”) (NASDAQ: PPHC), a leading global strategic communications provider offering a comprehensive range of advisory services in the areas of…
body_text: July 14, 2026 • News PPHC Strengthens Public Affairs Offering with Hire of Managing Director and Content Specialist WASHINGTON, July 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — PPHC (“the Company”) (NASDAQ: PPHC), a leading global strategic communications provider offering a comprehensive range of advisory services in the areas of Government Relations, Public Affairs and Corporate Communications, today announced that Seven Letter, a PPHC member company, has strengthened its New England and Washington, D.C. public affairs offering with the addition of Greg Honan as Managing Director in the firm’s Boston office and Esther Lynch as Content Specialist in Washington, D.C. The appointments come as Seven Letter, PPHC’s strategic communications agency with a specialty in bipartisan public affairs, approaches its 20th anniversary and continues to invest in senior talent. Honan’s combination of local government communications experience and service in the federal government — from Boston City Hall to the White House — supports both the firm’s growing Boston client base and its Washington, D.C. public affairs practice. Honan brings more than a decade of experience in politics, communications and media to Seven Letter. Deeply rooted in New England, he began his career at the Harvard Kennedy School advising the late David Gergen, former CNN Senior Political Analyst and Professor of Public Service. He went on to serve as Director of Message Planning and Special Assistant to the President at the White House, where he coordinated communications planning for events, trips and interviews for President Joe Biden, and as Chief of Staff to the White House Communications Director. He most recently served as Deputy Chief of Communications for the City of Boston, advising Mayor Michelle Wu and leading her communications, press, digital and speechwriting teams. Greg Honan will work out of Seven Letter’s Boston, MA office. Before his time in government, Honan served as Communications Director at With Honor Action and worked on the 2020 Democratic National Convention and the 2021 Presidential Inaugural Committee. He holds a B.A. in Political Science from Elon University and a master’s degree in public policy from the Harvard Kennedy School, where he was a John C. Culver Scholar and Belfer International and Global Affairs Student Fellow. “More than ever, clients are looking for counselors who bring extensive experience to the table and who have been in rooms when decisions are made. Greg’s work with Mayor Wu and his experience at the highest level of national politics is already benefiting our clients, and we are pleased to have him as part of our growing Boston practice and presence in New England,” said Drew O’Brien, Partner at Seven Letter. Lynch joins Seven Letter as a Content Specialist in the Washington, D.C. office, bringing experience across three continents. She has supported workforce access policy at Enable UK in Scotland, researched corporate social responsibility and human rights risk at the Mekong Club in Hong Kong, and contributed to ESG strategy at The Estée Lauder Companies. She joins Seven Letter after completing two semesters of the firm’s fellowship program. Lynch holds a degree in Political Science and Global Affairs from the University of Notre Dame and speaks English and French natively, with intermediate proficiency in Chinese. “Greg and Esther represent exactly the kind of talent that keeps Seven Letter moving forward. Greg Honan brings deep experience at the highest levels of government communications, and Esther Lynch has already proven herself around the world and in our competitive fellowship program. We are pleased to welcome them both to the team,” said Erik Smith, CEO and founding partner of Seven Letter. “Our continued investment in senior talent reflects the strength of Seven Letter and their focus on client service. Appointments of this caliber deepen the expertise available to clients across the Group,” said Stewart Hall, CEO of PPHC. About Seven Letter Seven Letter, a PPHC company, specializes in bipartisan public affairs, corporate communications, crisis management, message development and digital engagement, with offices in Washington, D.C., Boston, New York and Los Angeles. Seven Letter Labs combines technology-enabled audience targeting and award-winning creative content to shape reputation, market position and public policy among elite audiences. Seven Letter Insight, the firm’s in-house team of data scientists, blends the art and science of communication through qualitative and quantitative strategies to understand consumer intelligence and create and refine compelling narratives and persuasive messages. Seven Letter has been named to the PR News Agency Elite for the last five consecutive years and is a multi-year PR News “Top Places to Work” and PRWeek “Best Place to Work” award winner.
